title: Revisiting Local PageRank Estimation on Undirected Graphs: Simple and Optimal

problem.claim: Estimate the PageRank score of an arbitrary target node in an undirected graph with small relative error and high success probability.

gap.claim: The previous best upper bound was O(log n ⋅ min(dt, m1/2)) and came from a significantly more complex algorithm and analysis.

contributions.claim: BackMC is proposed as a simple algorithm for local PageRank estimation in undirected graphs, with a worst-case complexity upper bound of O(1/dmin ⋅ min(dt, m1/2)).
A matching lower bound of Ω(1/dmin ⋅ min(dt, m1/2)) is established for any algorithm solving local PageRank estimation.
Experiments are conducted on large-scale real-world and synthetic graphs, with BackMC reported as consistently superior.

stated_novelty.claim: Compared with the previous best upper bound, BackMC improves computational complexity by a factor of Θ(log n/dmin) while using a much simpler algorithm; the matching lower bound establishes theoretical optimality.

author_reported_evidence.claim: BackMC is reported to accurately estimate the target node's PageRank score with small relative error and high success probability.
BackMC is reported to consistently show superior performance on various large-scale real-world and synthetic graphs.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper proposes BackMC for local PageRank estimation on undirected graphs.
The algorithm has a worst-case upper bound of O(1/dmin ⋅ min(dt, m1/2)).
BackMC improves on the prior upper bound by Θ(log n/dmin) with a simpler algorithm.
A matching lower bound is established, supporting theoretical optimality.
Experiments on real-world and synthetic graphs report consistently superior performance.

source_observation.claim: A simpler algorithm is paired with an improved complexity upper bound and a matching lower bound.

interpretation.claim: Combining algorithmic simplification with tight complexity analysis can strengthen a method's theoretical contribution.

application.claim: When revisiting an established estimation problem, evaluate both whether the algorithm can be simplified and whether its complexity can be matched by a lower bound.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond undirected graphs or local PageRank estimation.

unknowns: The algorithmic details of BackMC are not provided.
The exact error and success-probability parameters are not specified.
Experimental datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not reported.
The proof techniques for the upper and lower bounds are not described.
